refs.title: Gaineswood at Demopolis, AL (constructed 1843-1861) - RuralSWAlabama
refs.note: Its account: 'Constructed over an 18 year period (1843-1861), Gaineswood evolved from a two-room "dogtrot" cabin into a Greek Revival style mansion. General Nathan Bryan Whitfield, the builder, was his own architect, though he had no formal training. The labor was done mostly by enslaved people, some of whom were extremely accomplished carpenters and plasterers. Three styles of Greek architecture are represented in the house: Doric-style outside, Ionic for the interior, and Corinthian in the drawing room.' It also states NRHP listing in 1972 and National Historic Landmark designation in 1973 and prints no reference number, so no `nrhp` ref is recorded rather than a guessed one.

note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for Tranche 2. The 1930s survey states NOT ONE DIMENSION -- no width, no depth, no ceiling height, no column count -- so nothing here can be held against the node's kit, and the six data pages are a historical sheet, an index of the 25 measured drawings and a quotation from a published book. The drawings themselves carry the figures (sheet 8 is a longitudinal section, sheet 9 the front elevation and plan of the north portico with 'baluatrocte censics® i§ad e&pitnl det&iXa'), and this container cannot read them. Worth carrying: the surveyor's index names porticoes on the north and south and a 'port© cosher' (porte cochere) on its own sheet, which is the node's 'columns on more than one elevation' tell recorded in 1934 without being called that; and the quoted authority makes the MEZZANINE the thing that deviates from type, where the node's diagnostic tells do not mention a mezzanine at all.
